newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank powers higher amid bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank powers higher amid bid talk.

text.p: Shares in Royal Bank of Scotland Plc rocketed in a surging UK bank sector on Friday, as an outbreak of bid speculation sparked fresh investment demand for a sector that has already risen sharply this year.
A Royal Bank spokeswoman dismissed the surge in the bank's shares as "just market speculation," while dealers said talk of a bid from HSBC Holdings Plc was at least two years old.
Yet Royal Bank shares had leapt 55-1/2p or 8.5 percent to 658 by 1012 GMT, the biggest gainer in the FTSE 100 by farg and helping drive the blue chip index to the latest of a series of record highs.
HSBC shares were up 65p at 18.60 stg. No-one at the Anglo-Hong Kong banking group, which owns Midland Bank in the UK, was immediately available for comment.
Other bank stocks also leapt, with Abbey National Plc, previously seen as a possible bid target as the sector consolidates, up 23p at 907-1/2, after earlier reaching a record 915p.

Barclays Plc was up 50p at 12.59 stg, Lloyds TSB Group Plc rose 11-1/2 at 614, Bank of Scotland Plc firmed 9p at 419, National Westminster Bank Plc gained 26-1/2p at 811-1/2 and Standard Chartered Plc rose 32-1/2p to 10.13 stg.

Recently-floated Alliance & Leicester Plc, expected to join the FTSE 100 index next month, also set the latest in a series of post-floation highs. It was up 18-1/2p at 645 by 0943 GMT, after earlier rising as high at 657p.
A report in the Financial Times helped ignite the sector's latest run, saying that the Royal Bank "would make an obvious target" for HSBC.

Yet dealers said much of Friday's surge in bank shares as a whole reflected continued attempts by investment funds to increase their holdings in the sector ahead of the flotation of the Halifax Building Society -- the UK's biggest mortgage lender -- next month.

"The point is that Halifax is going to have a market capitalisation of say 12 billion stg yet no institution is going to own a single share," said the head of equity trading at one top U.S. investment bank.
"Automatically it means everyone is going to be underweight the sector and that is creating a dramatic technical squeeze."
But he said the bank sector, which has dramatically outperformed the rest of the UK market in recent months, could see its bubble burst once the Halifax float was over.

"What we are seeing could be the sector's final flourish ahead of the Halifax issue," the head of trading said. "We are finding it difficult to justify buying some of these stocks at these sort of prices."
